what_its_for: Tetracaine is a numbing medicine (local anesthetic) used to temporarily numb a specific area of your body. It is commonly used in eye drops to numb the surface of the eye before eye exams or procedures, and it can also be used on the skin or mucous membranes (like the inside of the nose or throat) before certain medical procedures.
how_to_take: Use tetracaine exactly as directed by your doctor or healthcare provider. This medicine is usually given or applied by a healthcare professional in a medical setting. If you are using eye drops at home, wash your hands thoroughly before use. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket, and gently squeeze the prescribed number of drops into the pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Do not touch the tip of the dropper to your eye, fingers, or any other surface to avoid contamination. Do not rub your eyes after applying the drops.
dosing: The dose of tetracaine depends on the reason it is being used and the area being treated. Your doctor or healthcare provider will determine the right dose for you. For eye procedures, typically 1 to 2 drops are placed in the affected eye. Do not use more than directed. Never share this medication with anyone else.
missed_dose: Tetracaine is usually given as a single dose before a procedure, so a missed dose is generally not applicable. If you are using tetracaine on a scheduled basis at home and miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tetracaine at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep it between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Do not freeze eye drops. Keep the container tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired tetracaine safely — ask your pharmacist how to properly discard medications.
what_to_avoid: Do not rub or touch the numbed area while it is still numb, as you could accidentally injure yourself without feeling it. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after having your eyes numbed until your normal vision and feeling have fully returned. Do not wear contact lenses while your eyes are numb or until your doctor says it is safe to do so. Avoid using more tetracaine than prescribed, as too much can cause serious side effects. Do not use tetracaine if the solution appears discolored or cloudy.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following after using tetracaine: severe eye pain, redness, or swelling; a rash, hives, or itching; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; difficulty breathing or swallowing; dizziness, fast or irregular heartbeat; confusion or feeling faint; any unusual or worsening symptoms. Seek emergency medical help (call 911) if you think you are having a severe allergic reaction.
when_it_works: Tetracaine works very quickly. When used as eye drops, you should feel numbing within 30 seconds to 1 minute after the drops are applied. The numbing effect usually lasts about 10 to 20 minutes. Your healthcare provider will let you know when it is safe to resume normal activities after the numbing wears off.
special_populations: Children: Tetracaine may be used in children but only under close medical supervision. The dose will be adjusted based on the child's age and weight. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of tetracaine. Use with caution as directed by a doctor. Pregnant women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Use tetracaine during pregnancy only if clearly needed and directed by your doctor. Breastfeeding mothers: It is not fully known whether tetracaine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are breastfeeding. Patients with allergies: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to tetracaine, other 'caine' anesthetics (such as benzocaine or lidocaine), or any other medicines.
